source.title: Superposition as Lossy Compression: Measure with Sparse Autoencoders and Connect to Adversarial Vulnerability
source.authors: Leonard F. Bereska; Zoe Tzifa-Kratira; Reza Samavi; E. Gavves

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains a model on modular arithmetic and measures grokking-related training dynamics using feature counts and the Local Learning Coefficient (LLC), rather than identifying circuits as in the claim's proposed mechanism.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a grokking experiment and related feature-count and LLC dynamics. The accuracy trajectories appear only in Figure 6b, without numerical values or a textual description of their curves. Other results on algorithmic compression, adversarial training, and Pythia are not results about delayed generalization as specified in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper measures superposition with its own SAE-entropy metric. Grokking appears in one exploratory section, used as a testbed to show the metric detects a known transition. It does not vary training-set size or regime, does not identify circuits, and reports no accuracy numbers. The grokking curve itself is shown only in Figure 6b. The results are about the study's own measure, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right, but too narrow. The paper's main conclusions are that superposition can be measured as SAE-entropy effective features, and that adversarial training's effect on superposition depends on task complexity and capacity. The grokking result is an exploratory demonstration: feature count consolidates sharply at the transition while LLC decays smoothly. It is offered as evidence that the metric tracks developmental complexity, not as a finding about grokking.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses modular addition with 40% of possible pairs for training, a two-path MLP, and additionally measures SAE feature count and LLC. It reports no training-set-size sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-derived effective feature count shows sharp consolidation at the grokking transition and correlates with LLC (r=0.908). This concerns representational compression, not the timing or mechanism named by any version.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Superposition/effective-feature count drops sharply at the grokking generalization transition in a modular-addition MLP.

record.problems: The grokking experiment uses random seed 0 and one training-data fraction. Accuracy curves are shown only in a figure, without textual trajectory values; the reported feature-count and LLC measures are proxies and do not directly identify circuits.

untested.parts: Accuracy trajectories are figure-only. No training-set-size sweep, so the claim that the delay grows as data shrinks is untested.
No Fourier or other circuit is identified, there is no tracing of memorization removal, and no test of whether a continuous measure precedes the jump.
not tested (Pythia-70M analysis is layer-wise feature counts, not delayed generalization)
not tested (one weight decay value, 0.0002, with no sweep)

record.verdict_notes: The single-seed grokking run (40% of pairs, mod 53, weight decay 2e-4, 25k steps) was done by a co-author as a side experiment. The authors call all Section 6 findings preliminary and exploratory. No verdicts are given because no version is tested by the study's own claim-relevant measures.

versions.untested_parts: Only one modular-arithmetic training fraction is reported (40% of possible pairs); the effect of shrinking the training set is not tested. The text does not state when training accuracy saturates or quantify the test-accuracy trajectory.
The study measures feature count and LLC, but does not identify a Fourier circuit, directly trace memorizing components being removed, or establish that a generalizing circuit forms gradually.

rows.subject: two-path MLP
rows.size_stated: shared embeddings of dimension 12; hidden layer 48; output dimension 53
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition (a + b) mod 53 using sparse training data.
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy over training; generalization transition
rows.value: figure only; text places the generalization transition at epoch 60
rows.note: The figure plots training and test accuracy, but the text does not describe their values or trajectories. The stated epoch is the transition point, not a reported accuracy value.
rows.check: Figure only, with no train or test accuracy values or saturation time in the text. 'Epoch 60' is likely a checkpoint index (100 checkpoints, one every 250 of 25,000 steps), not a true epoch. This is a single seed at a single 40% fraction, so the delay-versus-data-size part of V1 cannot be read.

rows.subject: two-path MLP
rows.size_stated: shared embeddings of dimension 12; hidden layer 48; output dimension 53
rows.operation_detail: Measure feature-count dynamics during modular-arithmetic training.
rows.value: Feature count exhibits sharp consolidation precisely at the generalization transition (epoch 60).
rows.note: Feature count is a proxy for representation dynamics; the study does not identify the generalizing circuit itself.
rows.check: SAE effective-feature count is the study's own method being demonstrated, not a measure of circuit formation. It drops sharply at the transition, so it does not act as a continuous measure that anticipates the jump. Should not count as evidence on V2.

rows.subject: two-path MLP
rows.size_stated: shared embeddings of dimension 12; hidden layer 48; output dimension 53
rows.operation_detail: Estimate the Local Learning Coefficient (LLC) during training.
rows.value: Initial proliferation followed by smooth decay throughout training.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a complexity measure and contrasts its smooth trajectory with the sharp feature-count consolidation.
rows.check: LLC is described only as 'initial proliferation followed by smooth decay', with no values. The text does not show that it anticipates the accuracy jump or tracks a generalizing circuit. The reader's 'observed' state is unsupported.

rows.subject: two-path MLP
rows.size_stated: shared embeddings of dimension 12; hidden layer 48; output dimension 53
rows.operation_detail: Compare feature count and LLC across training.
rows.measure: Correlation between feature count and LLC
rows.note: This reports association between the two progress measures; it does not by itself show that either identifies a circuit or predicts the accuracy jump.
rows.check: The correlation r=0.908 between the study's metric and LLC validates the study's own method against another measure. It is not a result on any version, so it should not be a claim row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
